rounds.proof_sketch: For dim_size=4000, dim_idx reaches exactly 3 on final unrolled iteration. Original processes indices 3,2,1,0 via unrolled body; mutant processes same indices via cleanup loop. Both compute sum += input[3], output[3]=sum; sum += input[2], output[2]=sum; etc. in identical order. Operation sequence is mathematically identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop condition from >= to > at line 56, affecting whether dim_idx=3 enters the unrolled loop or cleanup loop. However, both code paths perform semantically identical computations: they process indices 3, 2, 1, 0 in that exact order, accumulating the same running sum and writing identical values to the output. The unrolled path pre-loads values but executes additions in the same sequence as the cleanup loop. Since floating-point operations are performed in the same order, there is no opportunity for numerical differences due to non-associativity.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable because the original unrolled path and the mutant's cleanup path execute mathematically identical operations in identical order. No input values can distinguish them.
rounds.recommendations: When testing loop unrolling mutations at boundary conditions, verify whether alternative code paths (unrolled vs scalar cleanup) are semantically equivalent before investing in value-based testing. Mutations that only shift work between equivalent code paths are inherently unkillable.
